lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say the Spanish sounds of table words clearly and greet a host or server politely.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Greet the host with buenas noches, say your name, ask how they are, and say three table words clearly.
lessons.title: Evening Greetings and Dinner Sounds
lessons.objective: Greet a restaurant host politely, give your name, and recognize common dinner words in Japanese script.
lessons.focus: こんばんは is an evening greeting; は is pronounced wa in わたしは. です makes a polite identification. Hiragana names ordinary words such as みず; katakana marks loanwords such as テーブル and メニュー. Read the kana and listen to their sound units. あ・い・う・え・お are the five vowel sounds; ん has its own beat, and ー lengthens a katakana vowel.
lessons.scene: Sam enters a small restaurant in Kyoto and greets the host.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Give the size of your group, a dinner time and simple quantities of wine, food and pesos.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the host how many people are in your group, what time your reservation is, and order 2 glasses of wine.
lessons.title: Numbers, Time, and Dinner Quantities
lessons.objective: Give a party size, reservation time, and simple food and drink quantities with Japanese counters and yen.
lessons.focus: Use 人 for people and 杯 for glasses. A reservation at 8:30 is 八時半; 一杯 and 二杯 count drinks. Prices are in 円. For food sold by weight, 百グラム names a 100-gram amount. Count from ゼロ through 十, 百, and 千 before applying the people and drink counters.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Describe dishes, tables and yourself with ser and estar at dinner.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the server where you are from, then say whether your dish is hot, cold, salty or delicious.
lessons.title: Identity, Location, and Food Condition
lessons.objective: Say where you are from, ask whether a terrace table is available, and describe a dish’s temperature, saltiness, spiciness, or taste.
lessons.focus: Japanese does not divide “to be” into Spanish ser and estar forms. カナダから来ました gives origin; テラスの席は空いていますか asks whether a seat is free. スープは冷たいです and 魚はおいしいです describe current food qualities. 休暇中です expresses being on vacation.

internalReviewNotes: Qualified Japanese review is required for naturalness, kana/kanji progression, pronunciation, counter forms, register, and variant answers.
The yen and 100-gram examples retain the Spanish lesson’s quantity purpose with Japan-specific units and currency.
No live runtime, offline pack, audio, or learner progress is changed.
Foundation 2–3 card-level readingKana supports early script decoding; qualified review should check every reading and add full Reader furigana before release.
